title: Abanyom language - Wikipedia
text: Abanyom, or Bakor, is a language of the Ekoid subfamily of Niger–Congo. It is spoken by the Abanyom people in the Cross River State region of Nigeria. A member of the Southern Bantoid group, Abanyom is fairly closely related to the Bantu languages.

title: Nkem-Nkum | Ethnologue Free
text: Nkem-Nkum is a stable indigenous language of Nigeria. It belongs to the Niger-Congo language family. The language is used as a first language by all in the ethnic community.

title: Nkem-Nkum language — Grokipedia
text: Nkem-Nkum, also known as Isibiri, is an Ekoid language belonging to the Niger-Congo language family, spoken primarily in the Ikom and Ogoja Local Government Areas of Cross River State, southeastern Nigeria. It has approximately 51,000 speakers (2008).
